newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical shares rise after strong Q1.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical shares rise after strong Q1.

text.p: Shares of U.S. Surgical Corp rose over eight percent Friday morning after the company's first quarter earnings exceeded Wall Street expectations.
Wasserstein Perella said analyst Robert Dunne upgraded his rating on the stock to buy from hold based on the stock's price.
Shares in the medical device company were up 2-3/4 to 35-1/8 after a delayed opening on the New York Stock Exchange.
After the market's close Thursday, U.S. Surgical reported first quarter earnings of $0.39 a share, which beat the First Call consensus estimate of $0.37.

U.S. Surgical Chairman Leon Hirsch told a meeting of industry analysts late Thursday that the company's 1997 revenues would be hurt by the strong dollar but that it still expected to meet Wall Street's 1997 earnings forecasts.
Analysts expect U.S. Surgical to earn $1.73 a share in 1997, according to First Call. The company earned $1.48 a share in 1996.
Salomon Brothers analyst Eli Kammerman reiterated a strong buy on the stock, calling the first quarter results "high quality."
"The company realized the combined benefits of healthy new product flow and improved productivity," Kammerman said in a report.
He cited contributions of new products including the ABBI breast biopsy system and the Ray spinal fusion cage.
